## Rule

Scale a 3×3 input cell-grid by factor N (N = count of non-background cells in 3×3), placing each cell in an N×N block. Output is [1,10,30,30] with the 3N×3N region filled and zeros beyond.

## Algorithm sketch

1. `Slice(input, [0,0],[3,3], axes=[2,3]) → input_3` [1,10,3,3]
2. Compute `N_scalar` = count of non-background cells in 3×3 (via ReduceSum over channels → Sub ch0 → ReduceSum spatial)
3. Live model: Select pre-built coordinate grid for N=2..8 via Equal+Where chain (7 grids, 6 n_consts)
4. `GridSample(input_3, selected_grid, nearest, align_corners=1, padding=zeros) → output` [1,10,30,30]

Grid encoding: grid[r,c] = (floor(c/N)-1, floor(r/N)-1) in normalized GridSample coords → output(r,c) = input_3(floor(r/N), floor(c/N)).

Removes 7 grids [1,30,30,2] and 6 n_const scalars (12606 params). 266/266 verify; adversarial 6592/6717 (98.1%) — shift 88.3% (N=9 edge case, not in normal inputs). | **STAGED** -25278 | 31014 | `task269_dyngridsample_t_HUGE_RSUM_e_on_5806_87` |

## Don't-do log

_Record ruled-out hypotheses here so future agents don't retry them._

- Do NOT apply fp16_selective: fp16 INCREASES cost by +14164 bytes (onnx converter adds extra Cast nodes). Verified by spread_scan.
- Do NOT use `(1-ch0)` to compute N_scalar: padding cells have ch0=0 so 1-ch0=1, causing overcounting. Use `ReduceSum(all_channels) - ch0` or the existing Sub(ReduceSum(input,axis=1), ch0) pattern.
- Adversarial shift mismatch 88.3% is due to N=9 edge case (all 9 cells nonzero): live uses grid_8 (scale 8), dynamic uses scale 9. This is benign — visible verify is 266/266 and N=9 is an adversarial edge case.
